title: Stoke Newington
intro: A Georgian village swallowed by London, with a park around a 1790s house, a wild Victorian cemetery, wetlands on old reservoirs and a high street of independent shops.

items.name: Clissold Park
items.blurb: A park around Clissold House, a villa of the 1790s, with lakes, an animal enclosure, a paddling pool and a café in the house.
items.tip: The café on the house's veranda is the classic Saturday stop.

items.name: Abney Park
items.blurb: A Victorian garden cemetery left to grow wild, now a woodland nature reserve with a ruined chapel at its heart.
items.tip: Enter from Stoke Newington High Street and head for the chapel.

items.name: Stoke Newington Church Street
items.blurb: A long, curving street of independent shops, bookshops, cafés and restaurants, with Georgian houses at the Clissold Park end.

items.name: Woodberry Wetlands
items.blurb: A reservoir turned into a nature reserve in 2016, with reed beds, birdlife and a café in the old Coal House.
items.tip: Free; the boardwalks are good for buggies.

items.name: St Mary's Old Church
items.blurb: A small parish church rebuilt in 1563, one of the few Elizabethan churches in London, facing the tall spire of the Victorian St Mary's across the road.
items.tip: The churchyard opens onto Clissold Park.

items.name: Newington Green Unitarian Church
items.blurb: Built in 1708 and the oldest nonconformist place of worship in London still in use, facing the small square of Newington Green.
items.tip: Newington Green has good cafés around it.
